items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: Charlie Barnet played that room... I'll never forget the first time... where I first heard Artie Shaw play in person... Charlie Barnet played that room

ctx.x: Guess you’re what they call a Life Member, right?

Yeah, Life Member. Very good, Monk. Yeah. I’ve been a member since 1939. They’re very nice, they take my dues every month. Yeah, they’re all right. But there was a lot of great music at one time. I’ll never forget the Lincoln Hotel on 46th, 47th Street and Eighth Avenue, I used to hear Artie Shaw’s band, or some band, some great band. Charlie Barnet played that room, Jan Savitt played that room. It was owned by a woman called Marie Cramer her name was. She owned these two hotels, the Lincoln Hotel on Eighth…

Lincoln Hotel she used all the “hot” bands like Artie Shaw and Charlie Barnet and Jan Savitt. I’ll never forget the first time, even though I adore Benny Goodman, where I first heard Artie Shaw play in person at the Lincoln Hotel, “Begin the Beguine.” It was unbelievable. That sound was just unbelievable the way the band came in. Buddy Rich on drums, Tony Pastor on saxophone, a very exciting sound, very exciting. And the band was right on, Monk. He had a very tight band. I’ll never forget when he was at the…
